subject: Graduated financial remedies & early-exit request for recurring latency events
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@finteq.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Finteq Procurement <procurement@finteq.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 1 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal — graduated financial remedies & early-exit for recurring latency events

Ben / team,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Finteq is excited about the integration potential, but procurement and legal have pushed back on reliance solely on credits as the only operational remedy for repeated performance failures. In particular, they asked whether we could agree to a graduated financial remedy that goes beyond one-off credits — something that creates meaningful incentives for rapid remediation and, if necessary, an early-exit mechanism tied to chronic latency regressions.

To be concrete, attached is a short summary (FTQ_requested_remedies_summary.pdf) outlining the types of incidents and outcomes Finteq is willing to accept: a staged financial exposure for repeated P95/P99 latency breaches, plus a capped early-exit right if incidents exceed a defined recurrence window. We do not expect unlimited liability, but we do need a path that moves beyond token credits where recurring degradation materially impacts revenue.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can consider:
- A defined severity ladder (3 tiers) with escalating fee-at-risk amounts (per-month cap)
- A 90–120 day recurrence window that triggers an early-exit right if N+ incidents occur
- A maximum aggregate cap (percentage of annual committed spend)

Happy to walk through the attached. If helpful, Liam (procurement) can join a call next week to run the approval checklist.

Thanks,

Jordan Lee
Sr. Sourcing Manager, Finteq
jordan.lee@finteq.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: FTQ_requested_remedies_summary.pdf (PDF, 2 pages)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@finteq.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 1 Jun 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal — graduated financial remedies & early-exit for recurring latency events

Jordan — thanks for the clear write-up and the attachment. I appreciate Finteq's need for stronger commercial levers where repeated latency materially harms customer-facing flows.

High level from our side: Redwood's standard practice is to offer service credits tied to SLO misses, with modest exceptions for capped fee exposure in larger enterprise deals. We try to avoid uncapped cash liabilities because the root cause analysis and remediation timelines vary (infrastructure, third-party infra, config, prompt shapes). That said, I believe there's room for a middle path that addresses Finteq's concern while keeping our operational risk bounded.

Attached is a sketch of a possible compromise (FTQ_proposed_schedule_v1.pdf) — severity bands with a small monthly fee-at-risk pool that increases only after multiple incidents and is expressly refundable as credits if a remediation plan meets agreed milestones. The intention is to create a meaningful economic signal while capping absolute cash exposure.

Next steps I propose:
- Marissa to review limits and redline SOW terms for legal acceptability.
- Neha to pull historical latency/uptime telemetry for our hosted prod region over the last 12 months (P95/P99) and share an anonymized summary so Finteq can calibrate thresholds.
- Quick alignment call Monday (30 min) with Liam/procurement + Jordan + Marissa + me. I can do 10:30–11:30 PT.

Open question for Finteq: would you accept a 90-day pilot with the staged pool in place while we gather telemetry and validate incident definitions? That would give both sides real data to inform a final cap.

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0104
Redwood Inference

Attachment: FTQ_proposed_schedule_v1.pdf (PDF, 3 pages)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@finteq.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 2 Jun 2028 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal — graduated financial remedies & early-exit for recurring latency events

Jordan / Ben — looping in a quick legal counterproposal so procurement has something formal to review. I have attached a redline of the SOW and a short note (redwood_sow_redline_20280602.docx). Key points from legal: 

1) Severity and root-cause. Any fee-at-risk or early-exit right must be triggered only after incidents are (a) measured against an agreed metric set (P95/P99 by endpoint/class), and (b) confirmed via joint RCA (to avoid crediting incidents caused by customer misconfiguration or third-party outages).

2) Gradation and cap. We are amenable to a tiered fee-at-risk pool but will cap aggregate exposure at a fixed percentage of committed spend over the contract year (we proposed 6% in the redline).

3) Cure and remediation. Before any early-exit becomes effective, Redwood should have an exclusive cure period with transparent remediation milestones and a neutral third-party arbiter for disputed root-cause determinations.

4) Pilot mechanics. We can accept a 90-day pilot during which the pool is held in escrow or tracked internally; if remediation meets the milestones, unused funds convert to credits. If not, limited cash transfer could occur under the capped amount.

Please review the redline and comment in-line. If Finteq can provide a sample incident that caused them material loss, that would help us calibrate the tier thresholds.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood_sow_redline_20280602.docx (Word doc, redline)
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@finteq.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Finteq Procurement <procurement@finteq.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Liam Ortiz <liam.ortiz@finteq.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Jun 2028 09:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal — graduated financial remedies & early-exit for recurring latency events

Marissa / Ben — thanks for the thoughtful options and the redline. I want to clarify Finteq's posture so we're aligned: our ask is not to increase day-to-day operational friction, it's about enterprise risk transfer. A handful of 10–30 second tail-latency events in our checkout/authorization flow in 2027 caused measurable revenue impact; procurement needs a contractual lever that is more immediate than a future credit ledger.

We are comfortable with:
- Joint RCA requirement (good to see in your note).
- A capped aggregated exposure (Finteq will accept a cap if it's predictable).
- A short pilot is acceptable if Redwood shares historical P95/P99 telemetry for the last 12 months for the region we plan to run in.

Attaching our procurement approval matrix for internal reviewers (finteq_procurement_matrix.pdf). We propose a call Tuesday 6 Jun at 10:00 PT to run through the redline and pilot parameters.

Jordan

Attachment: finteq_procurement_matrix.pdf (PDF, 4 pages)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@finteq.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Liam Ortiz <liam.ortiz@finteq.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Jun 2028 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal — graduated financial remedies & early-exit for recurring latency events

Jordan — appreciate the context and the matrix. Agreement path looks straightforward: 90-day pilot, jointly-agreed incident definitions, capped aggregated exposure, joint RCA. To make the pilot actionable today, we're offering the following compromise: 

- 90-day pilot where a staged fee-at-risk pool = 1.5% of committed monthly spend (escrowed or ledgered). Pool increases only after a second confirmed incident in the recurrence window.
- If Redwood meets remediation milestones within defined cure windows for incidents, unused pool converts to credits on a 2:1 ratio (i.e., some upside protection for Finteq).
- Early-exit right limited to once per contract year and only after joint RCA confirms provider root cause and a failure to meet remediation milestones.

I've uploaded a short slide with the mechanics and a DocuSign envelope to capture pilot acceptance: 90d-pilot-slide.png and https://docusign.com/envelope/ABCD-FTQ-2028. Can we lock the call Tuesday 10am PT? If so, I'll have Neha circulate the historical P95/P99 telemetry by EOD Tuesday so you have data in advance.

Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0104
